targets.en: United Kingdom: OPC legislative drafting English

instructions: Produce legally idiomatic translations, not word-for-word calques. Use the same defined term consistently. Preserve the source law, legal effect, actors, conditions, exceptions, negation, temporal scope, amounts, citations and all substantive content. Do not import Chinese or UK substantive law or replace Indonesian institutions with target-jurisdiction bodies. Keep source numbering, Article/paragraph/item hierarchy and all annexes. For Chinese use precise mainland normative legal usage: 应当 for obligations, 可以 for legal permission/discretion, 不得 for prohibitions, only when justified by the source; distinguish ability from permission and invalidity from repeal. Use 自…起施行 for commencement where accurate; distinguish making, promulgation and application dates. Render recitals naturally (e.g. 鉴于, 依据) without dropping them. Do not turn ministerial regulations into Chinese statutes or judgments. For English use clear, modern UK legislative drafting: must for duties, may for powers/permissions and must not for prohibitions where justified; avoid routine legislative shall, archaic calques and inflated wording. Prefer natural active clauses only when the actor is supported. Never replace semantic shall with mechanical substitutions. Preserve all tables, HTML tags and rowspan/colspan attributes, cell ordering, units, ranges and footnotes; translate textual labels and maintain the relationships. Do not guess unreadable OCR or uncertain terminology; retain clearly labelled uncertainty. Keep supplied editorial notes separate from law. These are unofficial translations; do not claim approval by a court or authority.
